Absolutely not! I don’t do that. But I am serious about what I said above that this particular topic is more suited for a real and complex discussion, and not for an appendix to a siddur.“So why did you include the question?” To show you that it is a good question! Chazal were careful how they worded things, so if they worded two

the way they did, there was a reason or many reasons, and the topic deserves study. And most certainly there are reasons why certain mitzvos and practices are different for men and women.“So you’re not going to say anything on this topic?” I’m going to present the approach that resonates with me. Of all the ideas and answers I have read and heard, this one works for me. But I am me, and you are not. And I don’t know what glasses you are wearing. I know what I’m writing, but I don’t know what you’re reading! If this helps, great! If not, also great! As I explained above, there are many approaches, all true on different levels, and you need the one that fits who you are.I know that was really a long introduction to the following short answer! But in this case, the introduction was more important than the answer itself.Here we go: We are all Hashem’s children. As children, all are beloved

That structure and defined “doing” of mitzvos, at specific times with specific objects, helps them focus on the spiritual and not get sidetracked from their mission.
